label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Rohan, fair question da. Sneha, no no, he gets to ask. He and Divya trusted me with 3 lakh of actual money, not LinkedIn “belief in the journey” points. I owe them a proper answer.

Short version: FixKaro is still a thing. Your money is at risk, but it is not gone. I can’t honestly tell you it’s safe or that you’ll definitely get it back. No need to start practising the sad face tonight, but I’m not going to give you a fake “all good bro” either.

What happened: the bridge round from the Hyderabad fund fell through on 28 Oct. The term sheet was basically ready, and I was expecting that money to come in. It didn’t. That left us needing to cut costs quite hard.

Last Friday we let go of 6 out of 14 people. Everyone got two months’ pay, and we’ve helped four of them get interviews already. Those are interviews, not offers yet. Firing people was the worst day of my life. I was going to say worse than failing maths in second sem, but honestly that doesn’t belong in the same category. These are good people who did nothing wrong.

After the cuts, we have about five months of runway. That’s where we stand now. We have time to try the narrower plan, not time to sit around waiting for a VC to rediscover his WhatsApp.

On that subject, one partner said “we love the energy” and then didn’t reply for 11 days. Apparently the energy was best appreciated from a distance.

The app has around 41k monthly users. Plumbers and electricians are growing, but AC servicing is bleeding money. So the plan is to shut AC servicing and focus on housing society tie-ups. Three societies in HSR have already signed pilots. That’s something concrete to work on, but pilots are not the same as a business that pays its own bills. We still have to prove this works.

I genuinely think we have a real shot with the societies. I also genuinely don’t know whether we’ll pull it off. Both things are true. I’d rather say that here than make you decode another post where I’m “humbled by the resilience of this incredible team”.

Your and Divya’s investment from the 2025 friends round is on the same terms as everyone else’s. Being my college friend unfortunately does not come with downside protection. It does come with the right to ask uncomfortable questions without anyone telling you to let me breathe.

Let’s do a proper call this week, all three of us. I’ll show you the numbers, the cash we have, what we’re spending and what the society plan needs to deliver. Divya shouldn’t have to get her answers through your dinner-table impression of my LinkedIn post.

And yes, I’m fine. Not enjoying this bit, obviously, but I’m fine. I eat Maggi at the office at 11pm so often that security uncle now asks “masala or plain?” Amma has also asked whether TCS is still hiring, so the family has opened a parallel strategic review.

Coming Saturday. Please don’t make it a founder condolence meeting. I want dosa, beer and to hear about somebody else’s problems for a change.

Pranav is buying. That funding commitment, at least, we can settle in this group.
